newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Krasnoyarskenergo defends hydro stake sale.
newsitem.headline: Russian Krasnoyarskenergo defends hydro stake sale.

text.p: Russian regional utility Krasnoyarskenergo, attacked by a cabinet official for selling a stake in its major asset last year, defended its move on Wednesday by saying it had done nothing wrong.

First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov criticised the utility earlier this week for selling 20 percent of its unit Krasnoyarsk Hydroelectric Station, saying the stake in the core plant went too cheaply.

"I acted within the boundaries of my competence," Krasnoyarskenergo general director Vladimir Ivannikov said by telephone. "It is in somebody's interests to misinform, putting it mildly, the deputy prime minister."

Nemtsov said on Monday in Novosibirsk that the stake in the hydroelectric plant, the second biggest of its kind in Russia, had been sold for 14 billion roubles ($2.4 billion at currently lower rates) but was actually worth $8 billion.
The hydroelectric plant accounts for 75 percent of Krasnoyarskenergo's electricity output.
Ivannikov said the stake was sold to local firm TONAKO, which comprises Krasnoyarskenergo, the Krasnoyarsk aluminium smelter, Achinsky oil refinery, Achinsky alumina plant and Metaleks Bank.
The sale, along with others, reduced Krasnoyarskenergo's 51.9 percent holding in the hydroelectric station, to 27.9 percent.
National utility UES, a central target of Nemtsov's restructuring efforts owns a controlling stake in Krasnoyarskenergo.
